scope: F — Remaining Clinical first-learning cognition, Source contact, retrieval closure, compression and repair return
medical_core_owner: 9 canonical F Block Markdown files under content/xizong/knowledge/systems/f-remaining-clinical/blocks/
role: System-specific Learning candidate for F. It decides learner order, Source-contact granularity, Logic Groups, retrieval closure, compression and repair return without rewriting accepted F medical Knowledge.
rule: Preserve the accepted dual-context F Knowledge model. Acute disturbance-control and planned intervention-safety share coordinates but do not become one serial learner workflow; F9 remains ownership-first and low-connectivity.

classes.WHOLE_BLOCK_SOURCE: one compact coherent original-Lecture unit is consumed continuously before local retrieval
classes.NATURAL_SOURCE_UNITS: a multi-center Block uses a small number of genuine Source sub-units; each Source unit may support several Logic Groups
classes.INTEGRATION_PRIMARY: KianOS owns ownership split/integration/retrieval while original Source is revisited selectively for residual Micro Primary, decisive visuals or exact wording

source_contact_contract.hard_rule: Logic Group count never determines Source-contact count. VISUAL_REQUIRED is evidence/closure, not automatically a separate handoff.

units: systemic burn mechanism + area/depth/severity visual formation
time-phase + fluid-resuscitation logic; exact first-day formula remains original-Source visual / fail-closed
post-anesthesia positioning + routine recovery / suture-drain timing
postoperative time/system/evidence deviations: fever, pulmonary, urinary, bleeding and GI recovery

targeted_source: laparoscopy Current Source / missing complication visual

visual_contract.rule: Spatial, procedural-space or morphology-dependent cognition requires real original-Source visual contact where Current Source owns it; prose cannot certify never-seen visual relations.
visual_contract.open_debt: F3–F9 retain mounted-page/visual limitations where declared; F1/F2 require original Source review for selected exact mappings. L preserves these constraints rather than manufacturing closure.

negative_space: F1 selected poison-manifestation exact mappings remain Source-bounded; no model-prior completion
F2 delayed polyneuropathy/rebound exact wording remains Source-bounded
F3 delayed-primary/secondary-closure taxonomy detail and live Source conflict remain explicit
F4 complete first-day burn-fluid coefficient/body-weight-area/intraday distribution remains fail-closed
F5 Study threshold conflicts such as hypertension remain explicit
F9 complete laparoscopy complication list remains Source gap

no silent modernization into full modern toxicology, burn-center, ERAS/ICU, difficult-airway/MAC/extubation, ultrasound-guided regional/LAST, transplant, dermatopathology or full pharmacology curricula
no duplicate shock/perfusion, airway/respiratory failure, renal/fluid, liver/nutrition, infection/sepsis/transfusion, NMJ/neural or tumor-general Primary
no inferred official F System question membership while S2 remains UNTESTED
no learner progress/mastery claim from repository construction

repair_return.acute_threat_or_control_failure: smallest failed F1–F4 Logic Group; separate support from source/specific control
repair_return.intervention_safety_failure: smallest failed F5–F8 Logic Group; localize urgency/reserve/function/space/iatrogenic-risk layer
repair_return.visual_relation_missing: return to original visual Source; if Source remains missing, preserve debt rather than certify mastery
repair_return.external_owner_baseline_missing: smallest-sufficient owner/Chat repair without rebuilding the external System inside F
repair_return.source_gap_or_conflict: Current Source-context check; do not choose a value/list from model prior
repair_return.return_rule: after repair, return to the interrupted F mainline; repair evidence does not erase the original observation or prove mastery

F1: A1/A2/A3 immediate support interfaces where already learned
F9: true external owners first; F1–F8 only when a residual case actually needs them

system_route.external_missing_rule: If an external baseline has not actually been learned, use the smallest-sufficient repair for the current F action; do not manufacture learner completion or a hard repository dependency.
system_route.hard_edge_rule: A hard inside-F edge is allowed only if a later Block intentionally consumes an earlier F model, does not rebuild it, and bounded reactivation is insufficient. Builder review finds no such edge; fresh audit must actively attack this zero-edge claim.
system_route.flex_rule: The default route minimizes switching across toxicology → general surgery/barrier injury → perioperative → anesthesia → residual tail. Useful comparison or source continuity is not hard legality. F9 remains ownership-first rather than the endpoint of a fake unified chain.

first_pass_chain: System orientation in KianOS using the accepted dual-context F model
bounded Block / natural Source-unit orientation and stop-line
continuous original Lecture contact for genuine new Source learning; F9 uses integration-primary ownership split with targeted Source return
one normal return after the relevant Source contact rather than one handoff per LG
active KP retrieval by accepted Logic-Group learner order
Logic-Group closure; exact/visual Source gaps remain fail-closed
after all Block LGs close: Block Recall
optional non-gating Partial-System Reconstruction after the acute-control branch and intervention-safety branch
after all 9 Blocks are actually learned: final F System Reconstruction including F9 ownership split
trusted official F System question sweep only after S2 exact official-question membership separately closes
Wrong / Uncertain returns through the smallest failed LG, exact Source, visual Source, precision object or external owner

partial_system_reconstructions.target: harmful input / contamination / tissue injury → immediate threat → support + conditional source/removal control → bounded specific control → iatrogenic risk → recovery/deviation
partial_system_reconstructions.closure: route a new acute non-organ-specific disturbance by threat and control layer without collapsing support into source control

partial_system_reconstructions.target: urgency + physiologic reserve → intended intervention/anesthetic function + action space → support/monitoring → iatrogenic risk → recovery/deviation
partial_system_reconstructions.closure: route a planned or ongoing intervention by safety layer without misclassifying the intervention itself as a harmful source

F1.goal: prioritize immediate physiologic danger, then identify exposure route and high-value respiratory/pupil direction
F1.closure: for a new poisoning presentation, state what threatens life first and which exposure/clue layer is being used before naming the toxicant

F1.goal: use odor, skin/corrosive appearance and organ manifestations as weighted clues rather than diagnosis shortcuts
F1.closure: combine several clue classes and identify the damaged physiologic layer without letting one sensory clue overrule threat-first care

F1.goal: separate not-yet-absorbed decontamination from already-absorbed poison management and recognize when a procedure creates more harm
F1.closure: choose a decontamination action only after route/timing/contraindication analysis

F1.goal: separate dialysis, hemoperfusion and plasma exchange by physicochemical mechanism and indication
F1.closure: given a toxin property profile, choose the elimination modality or reject extracorporeal removal rather than using 'poisoning = dialysis'

F1.goal: attach antidotes to toxic effect/target while preserving the final threat-first exposure-control algorithm
F1.closure: reconstruct support → exposure/decontamination → elimination/antidote logic without letting antidote lists replace stabilization

F2.goal: derive M/N1/N2/CNS findings and respiratory danger from AChE inhibition, then grade severity by layer involvement
F2.closure: explain why cholinergic crisis can kill through overlapping respiratory mechanisms and distinguish mild/moderate/severe without symptom counting

F2.goal: separate exposure removal, atropinic control, cholinesterase reactivation and treatment toxicity
F2.closure: for ongoing cholinergic toxicity, assign each treatment to its control layer and distinguish under-treatment, atropinization and atropine toxicity

F2.goal: preserve the post-acute timeline where intermediate or delayed respiratory/neural risk can appear
F2.closure: state why apparent acute improvement does not automatically close observation and which later syndrome timing remains Source-bounded

F2.goal: use opioid/sedative comparisons only as bounded toxicology interfaces
F2.closure: recognize the minimum opioid/sedative pattern and antidote direction without expanding F2 into full pharmacology

F3.goal: distinguish sterilization vs disinfection and match methods to material/organism constraints
F3.closure: given an item/pathogen constraint, choose the correct sterility method and justify the sterilization/disinfection boundary

F3.goal: maintain operative-field direction/boundaries and respond correctly to contamination or special pathogens
F3.closure: identify when the sterile field is broken and choose the smallest corrective action without inventing extra protocol

F3.goal: prioritize life-threatening bleeding, then restore viable tissue boundaries through hemostasis and debridement
F3.closure: route an open wound through danger → hemostasis → viability/contamination rather than starting with skin closure

F3.goal: decide primary closure eligibility from time/location/contamination while preserving unresolved closure-taxonomy Source limits
F3.closure: choose primary closure vs leave open using Current Source-supported criteria and fail closed on unresolved exact taxonomy

F4.goal: connect endothelial leak to edema/shock and preserve the Study stress-ulcer interface
F4.closure: explain the early systemic burn threat before entering area/depth calculations

F4.goal: separate area, depth and severity/upgrading factors
F4.closure: classify a burn on independent area/depth axes and derive severity without using one number as the whole model

F4.goal: map burn phases and early fluid-resuscitation logic while keeping the unresolved exact first-day formula fail-closed
F4.closure: identify the current burn phase and resuscitation objective without fabricating missing exact formula coefficients

F4.goal: integrate infection-source reduction, transport, blister-skin handling and coverage choice
F4.closure: choose early wound/source-control direction from burn depth/site rather than treating antibiotics as sufficient

F4.goal: recognize inhalation injury and run the whole burn decision sequence
F4.closure: route airway → area → depth → severity → phase → resuscitation/wound care for a new burn case

F5.goal: separate emergency/limited/elective timing and combine urgency with physiologic reserve/reversible risk
F5.closure: make a go-now vs optimize-first decision without delaying time-sensitive surgery for ideal physiology

F5.goal: handle smoking/alcohol/stroke timing and liver/renal reserve as bounded preoperative risk modifiers
F5.closure: identify which reserve deficit changes timing and which can be optimized without inventing new specialty guidance

F5.goal: apply fasting and GI/bowel preparation to reduce aspiration/infectious risk
F5.closure: choose preparation from procedure/food category while preserving Current Study timing

F5.goal: manage diabetes, hypertension, NSAID/antiplatelet timing and platelet thresholds without collapsing distinct risk domains
F5.closure: for a preop medication/lab issue, identify the risk being controlled and preserve explicit Source conflicts instead of reconciling them from prior knowledge

F5.goal: place skin prep at the correct time and integrate urgency, decompensation, aspiration, bleeding, infection and healing risk
F5.closure: run a final go/delay decision that is urgency-constrained rather than checklist-maximalist

F6.goal: position, mobilization context, suture removal and drain removal as expected recovery coordinates
F6.closure: given operation/site/device timing, choose the expected routine recovery action without turning it into a universal rule

F6.goal: use time + organ/system + evidence to distinguish fever, pulmonary, urinary, bleeding and GI recovery deviations
F6.closure: localize a postoperative deviation by timing and failed system before naming the complication

F6.goal: separate contamination class from healing outcome grade
F6.closure: classify incision contamination and healing outcome as two different axes

F6.goal: distinguish hematoma/seroma, infection and dehiscence and choose source-control/closure response
F6.closure: identify the wound complication from fluid/inflammation/mechanical failure and route the smallest corrective action

F7.goal: separate anesthesia functions from preop metabolic/premedication context and airway protection
F7.closure: state which function is missing—hypnosis, analgesia, reflex suppression, relaxation, airway/ventilation or hemodynamic support—before choosing a drug

F7.goal: use blood/gas control plus inhaled/IV drug profiles as selection dimensions
F7.closure: compare anesthetic agents by controllability/role rather than memorizing a flat list

F7.goal: separate muscle paralysis from consciousness/analgesia and distinguish nondepolarizing vs depolarizing N2 blockade
F7.closure: predict muscle-relaxant effect/reversal while explicitly stating what muscle relaxation does not provide

F7.goal: compress representative agent pairing into the six-function/risk model
F7.closure: for a general-anesthesia scenario, identify intended function, missing support layer and major iatrogenic risk before selecting the representative agent

F8.goal: classify local/regional techniques by drug space and adjacent anatomy, including epinephrine boundaries
F8.closure: predict benefit and complication from where the anesthetic is deposited rather than from drug name alone

F8.goal: connect active free drug, ester/amide identity and physicochemical properties to onset/duration/toxicity
F8.closure: explain a local-anesthetic profile from mechanism/class/property instead of memorizing isolated pairs

F8.goal: compare representative local anesthetics and preserve high-density dose limits as precision
F8.closure: choose a representative agent from intended use/duration/safety while keeping exact limits as bounded precision

F8.goal: separate subarachnoid vs epidural space, block order, surface level and plane-control variables
F8.closure: derive block extent and physiologic consequences from intervention space/depth and level

F8.goal: recognize total spinal/typical spinal complications and distinguish sacral vs saddle approaches
F8.closure: map a complication or perineal technique back to the space/level that produced it

F9.goal: separate external-owner transplant/tumor/cancer-pain/drug truth from true residual F Primary
F9.closure: route each residual topic to its real owner before learning anything new under F9

F9.goal: retain only the bounded CO2-pneumoperitoneum/laparoscopy interface while the complete complication list remains Source gap
F9.closure: state the minimum laparoscopy-specific F Primary and explicitly fail closed on the missing full complication list

F9.goal: distinguish basal-cell carcinoma, melanoma and junctional nevus using behavior/location/morphology warning axes
F9.closure: identify malignant-warning direction from behavior and morphology without rebuilding full dermatopathology

F9.goal: classify lipoma, sebaceous cyst and dermoid cyst then use a six-axis surface-mass algorithm
F9.closure: localize a superficial mass by site/consistency/skin sign/content/depth/behavior before malignancy escalation

compression.ladder: 121 KP → 40 LG → 9 Block Recall → 2 non-gating PSR → final F System Reconstruction
compression.block_recall_rule: rebuild the governing disturbance/intervention problem; do not recite KP labels

final_system_reconstruction.target: choose acute-disturbance vs intervention-safety context; localize threat/support/source-or-specific-control/space/iatrogenic-risk/recovery; then split F9 ownership before residual Micro Primary
forbidden: treat planned surgery/anesthesia as a harmful source to terminate
claim exact Source-gap or visual mastery from model prior/prose
force F9 into one common mechanism

compression.second_pass: decisive discriminations + high-value precision + procedural/visual relations + cases + Wrong/Uncertain/fresh verification; do not replay all 40 LGs by default
compression.late_review: dual-context mother model + two PSR skeletons + F9 ownership split + real weak points + exact Source/visual debt

outputs: cross-System threat-first stabilization + conditional source control
perioperative urgency/reserve context for organ-specific surgery
anesthesia function/space/risk language for later integration
cross_system_handoff.fine_grain_rule: System-level interfaces are allowed; finer external Block/KP routing fails closed without separately reviewed Current authority.

projection_boundary.rule: Projection may not rewrite F Learning Logic to fit file order, contiguous LG ranges, or an organ-style workflow.
